subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this opt-in per-maintenance timeout, generic queue timeout callback, and host-side abandonment fence as the permanent contract for non-cooperative context-engine maintenance?
rationale: The code can implement several coherent policies, but source inspection cannot decide whether maintainers want a new config surface and generic queue callback, an existing shared safety budget, or no host abandonment of plugin work.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep the new config, synchronous queue hook, persistence checkpoint, and host-owned fences, then merge after rebasing and restoring green checks.

options.title: Reuse a shared safety budget
options.body: Rework maintenance around the existing compaction safety timeout and define compatible default behavior without adding a separate operator setting.

options.title: Reject host abandonment
options.body: Keep maintenance unbounded in core and address lock contention, cancellation, and batching through the context-engine plugin contract instead.

recommendation.title: Approve the opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Keep the new config, synchronous queue hook, persistence checkpoint, and host-owned fences, then merge after rebasing and restoring green checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the shared context-engine lifecycle across harnesses, making them the strongest available owner for the permanent lifecycle contract.
